purpose: Define how `callisto version`, `pre` and `snapshot` turn pending changesets and commits into new package versions, dependency rewrites, changelog sections and an optional release decision file.
scope: Changeset file format, severity aggregation and commit inference, dependency cascade, fixed and linked groups, prerelease and snapshot versions, and applying the plan to disk.
non_goals: Publishing, tagging, and verifying a committed release decision during `release`.
Package discovery, workspace config parsing and dependency graph construction.

api_surface.name: callisto version
api_surface.description: Computes the version plan from pending changesets, inference, cascade and groups, then applies it to disk and stages it in git.

api_surface.name: callisto pre
api_surface.signature: callisto pre enter <TAG> | callisto pre exit
api_surface.description: Enters or exits prerelease mode by writing `.changeset/pre.json`.

api_surface.name: callisto snapshot
api_surface.description: Sets every package to a throwaway `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}` version without consuming changesets.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A changeset is a Markdown file whose line 1 is `---`, followed by one `name: severity` entry per line, a closing `---` line and a free-text summary; blank lines and lines starting with `#` inside the frontmatter are ignored. Severities are `major`, `minor`, `patch` and `none` (ordered none < patch < minor < major), read case-insensitively and written lowercase.
A package name may be double-quoted, and a quoted name may contain `:` (`"maven/org.example:foo-core": major` parses as that name with severity major); an unquoted name is split at its last `:`.
A leading UTF-8 BOM is ignored, CRLF and CR line endings parse the same as LF, the summary is trimmed of surrounding whitespace, and a changeset with a summary but no entries is valid.

Parsing fails with E040 when line 1 is not `---`, E041 when the frontmatter is never closed, E048 when there are no entries and no summary, and E055 when there are entries but the summary is empty or whitespace-only.

Parsing fails on a bad entry line and reports its line number: unclosed quoted name (E042), text between a quoted name and its `:` (E043), no `:` (E044), empty name (E045), unknown severity (E046), or a name already used in the same file (E047, also citing the first line).

Writing a changeset emits `---`, one `name: severity` line per entry in order, `---`, a blank line, the trimmed summary and a trailing newline; a name is quoted when it starts with a YAML-significant character (such as `@`, `-`, `#`, `"` or a space), contains `:` or `#`, or ends with a space.
Writing fails for an empty summary (E049 with no entries, E056 with entries), an empty package name (E057), or a name containing `"`.

`version` reads every `.md` file directly inside the configured changesets directory (default `.changeset`) except `README.md`, in path order; a missing directory means no changesets, and one unparsable file aborts the run with an error naming that file.
A package's severity is the highest severity among all changeset entries naming it and its inferred severity.

An entry name resolves to a workspace package by prefixed id (`cargo/foo`) or bare name; a bare name that matches packages in two or more ecosystems aborts the run with an ambiguous-name error (E103).

An entry naming a package not in the workspace, or an invalid name, produces an unknown-package warning, and a changeset in which no entry resolves stays on disk unconsumed. An entry with severity `none` causes no bump and no changelog line, but its changeset is still consumed.

Commit inference runs only for packages with `release-trigger = "auto"`; packages with the default `release-trigger = "changeset"` take severity from changesets alone. Inference reads conventional commits touching the package's directory since its last release tag (all history when untagged): a `!` marker or `BREAKING CHANGE`/`BREAKING-CHANGE` footer maps to major, `feat` to minor, `fix`/`perf`/`revert` to patch, anything else to none.

`pre-major-inference` changes only inferred severity, and only for a package with a prior release tag whose current version is `0.y.z` with y >= 1: `conservative` maps major to minor, `conservative-feat` also maps minor to patch, and `off` (default) changes nothing.

When no changeset is consumed, `version` warns "No pending changesets found in workspace" unless `--allow-empty-changesets` or `[validation] allow-empty-changesets = true` is set; with `--strict` the warning is an error and `version` exits with a failure status.

When a package is bumped, each dependent's spec on it is tested against the new version. Under `[cascade] mode = "out-of-range"` (default) a runtime, optional, build or peer dependent is bumped only when its spec no longer covers the new version; under `mode = "always"` it is bumped regardless. Coverage governs only the dependent's own severity bump; whether its spec is rewritten follows VER-CAS-06.
A cascaded bump has severity `bump-severity` (`patch` default, or `minor`), never lowers a severity the dependent already has, and propagates to that dependent's own dependents.

With `peer-escalation = true` (default), a peer dependent whose spec no longer covers a minor or major bump of its dependency receives a major bump; a patch bump of the dependency cascades at `bump-severity`.
A dev dependent is never bumped by the cascade, but its spec is still rewritten when it no longer covers the new version.

Coverage: an exact spec covers only the equal version, a bare Cargo version is a caret requirement, a caret requirement never covers a prerelease, a Cargo `workspace = true` spec is tested using the root `[workspace.dependencies]` spec, and an npm `workspace:` spec always covers. A catalog or other untestable spec is treated as covering and never rewritten; a catalog spec emits a CatalogSpecNotRewritten warning.

A spec that no longer covers the new version is rewritten to it, keeping the operator and precision for Cargo and npm (`^1.2` becomes `^2.0` for 2.0.0), or to the exact version for npm when `preserve-npm-ranges = false`. A runtime, optional, build or peer dependent that is itself released in this run, for any reason, has every such spec on a bumped internal dependency raised to the dependency's new version the same way, even when the spec still covers it; a dependent that is not releasing keeps its spec unless out of range. `workspace = true`, npm `workspace:` and catalog specs are never rewritten by either rule, and a dev dependent's spec is rewritten only when out of range. A spec that cannot be rewritten mechanically, such as an npm range with spaces, `||`, a hyphen or a wildcard, is left unchanged with a RangeNotRoundTrippable warning.

A rewrite names the dependency as the dependent's own ecosystem spells it, so an npm dependent of a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names is rewritten under the npm name. A Cargo dependency inherited with `workspace = true` is rewritten in the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]`, not in the member manifest.

The cascade aborts with E105 when it does not settle within 4 x (package count) + 1 steps, and with a grammar-mismatch error when a spec and the new version use different version grammars (SemVer vs PEP 440).

All package members of a `[[fixed-group]]` receive the group's highest severity and one shared version, computed the same grammar- and pre-release-aware way as any other bump (VER-PRE-03): the alignment base is the on-disk version of the group's released member (a member with a release tag) if the group has one, otherwise the highest on-disk version among its members, bumped by that severity.

A fixed group whose released members have different on-disk versions aborts the run with E106, one whose released members use different version grammars (or whose untagged members do) aborts with E107, one whose released member has no on-disk base version aborts with E205, and one with no live member carrying a base version aborts with E206.

A computed bump — for a single package or a fixed group's shared target — that would sort behind the version it was bumped from aborts the run with E207 instead of writing the regressed version to disk.

When any member of a `[[linked-group]]` is bumped, every member receives the group's highest severity and all members move to the highest version any member's own bump produces (members at 1.4.0 and 2.7.3 with a minor bump both become 2.8.0).
A package claimed by two groups is rejected: E109 when the claims use different spellings of the same package, and a group-conflict error when they use the same spelling.

An attached platform package, or a fixed-group member naming a platform manifest, is not bumped as a package: when its owner is bumped, the platform manifest gets the owner's new version and the owner's `optionalDependencies` entry for it is pinned to that version. A co-located platform manifest that is also one of the owner's canonical manifests is written once, as part of the owner's own bump.

`callisto pre enter <tag>` writes `.changeset/pre.json` with `mode` `pre`, the tag, every package's current version under `initialVersions` and an empty `changesets` list, then stages the file with git; under `--dry-run` it prints the content and writes nothing.

`pre enter` fails when the tag is empty or whitespace or `.changeset/pre.json` already exists (also under `--dry-run`); `callisto pre exit` sets `mode` to `exit` and fails when the file is missing or already in `exit` mode.

In pre mode, a bumped package's version is its `initialVersions` entry bumped by its severity plus `-{tag}.N`, where N starts at 0 and increments while the release part is unchanged (0.1.0 with a minor changeset and tag `beta` gives 0.2.0-beta.0, then 0.2.0-beta.1); PEP 440 packages use `aN` for tags `a`/`alpha`, `bN` for `b`/`beta`, `rcN` for `rc`/`c`/`pre`/`preview` (case-insensitive), and `.devN` for any other tag.

In pre mode, `version` never deletes a changeset from disk. A changeset whose id is not yet in `pre.json`'s `changesets` list counts toward severity, produces a changelog entry, and has its id added to `changesets`; a changeset whose id is already there still counts toward severity and the prerelease counter (VER-PRE-03) but produces no additional changelog entry. The `allow-empty-changesets`/`--strict` handling from VER-AGG-06 triggers only when no changeset -- new or already recorded -- resolves to a package this run, not merely when nothing new was added.

After `pre exit`, the next `version` moves every package at a prerelease version to its stable release (0.2.0-beta.1 becomes 0.2.0), consumes and deletes the pending changesets, and deletes `pre.json`.

A malformed `.changeset/pre.json` (invalid JSON, a missing `mode`, `tag`, `initialVersions` or `changesets` field, a mode other than `pre` or `exit`, or an unparsable version) makes `version` fail with E114 and write nothing; an unreadable file fails with E115.

`callisto snapshot --tag <tag>` sets every workspace package, and every attached platform package and fixed-group platform manifest, to the single version `0.0.0-{tag}-{sha7}`, where sha7 is the first 7 characters of HEAD; it fails if HEAD cannot be resolved.
A snapshot writes manifests only: it ignores and keeps pending changesets, writes no changelog or `pre.json`, and stages nothing in git; under `--dry-run` it writes nothing.

For every workspace dependency whose current spec does not cover the snapshot version, `snapshot` rewrites that spec in the dependent's own manifest, using the dependent's ecosystem and the dependency's name as registered for that ecosystem; a spec that already covers the snapshot version is left unchanged.
`version` writes the new version to every canonical manifest of a bumped package, so both manifests of a dual-manifest package move together.

Before writing a package or platform manifest, apply reads its current version: equal to the planned `from` it is written, equal to the target it is left unchanged, so applying the same plan again is safe.
A manifest whose current version is neither the planned `from` nor the target aborts apply with E117 naming the path, the found version and both expected versions.

A manifest that receives a version bump and dependency rewrites in the same run is read once and written once with all changes, and a manifest already at its target with no rewrites is not rewritten. An owner's `optionalDependencies` pins, and edits to a workspace root `Cargo.toml` that is also a package manifest, are written separately.
Files are written one at a time, each by atomic replacement, so an interrupted run never leaves a partially written file; a failing write stops the run and leaves earlier files in place.

For each bumped package, apply prepends a `## {version}` section under the `# {package}` heading of its changelog (default `CHANGELOG.md` in the package directory, overridable with `changelog`), creating the file if missing and keeping CRLF line endings; a changelog that already has that heading is left unchanged.

A changelog section lists each changeset summary as a bullet (continuation lines indented), an inferred bump as a commit subject with its short sha, a group bump as "Released together with the `{group}` {fixed|linked} group.", a new fixed-group member as "Joined the `{group}` group at this version.", a peer escalation as "Peer dependency `{dep}` requires `{version}`", and cascaded bumps as "`{dep}` → `{version}`" lines under a "Dependency updates" bullet.

Outside pre mode, a successful `version` deletes the consumed changeset files, then stages every written manifest and changelog, `pre.json` changes, the existing lockfiles of affected ecosystems, and the changeset deletions (via `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch`, which also succeeds for an already-deleted file).
`version --dry-run` prints the computed plan (text output starts with `[DRY-RUN]`) and writes, deletes and stages nothing.

`version --emit-decision <path>` writes the release decision JSON to `<path>` relative to the workspace root after the plan has been applied successfully: `schemaVersion` 2, a digest, and one entry per canonical manifest of each bumped package (ecosystem-qualified name, target version, reasons) sorted by package. Reason `kind` is `changeset`, `inference`, `fixedGroup` or `linkedGroup` (with `groupId`), `cascade` (with source package and edge kind, `peer` for peer escalation) or `preReleasePolicy` (with the prerelease tag).

`--emit-decision` with `--dry-run` is rejected before any work, and a plan with no bumps, or whose group members have different target versions, fails to produce a decision before any file is written.

A diagnostic escalated to an error (for example `--strict` on the empty-changeset warning) is evaluated right after planning: `version` writes nothing -- not the manifests and changelog, not `pre.json`, not the `--emit-decision` file -- and exits with a failure status, instead of applying the plan and only then failing.

After planning but before any write, `version` refuses with E121 when a canonical manifest's on-disk version differs from its version at `HEAD` and either: the workspace's changesets directory still has a pending changeset as of `HEAD` (not yet consumed by a commit); or, outside an active pre-release cycle (`.changeset/pre.json` absent), a canonical manifest is staged in the git index but not yet committed. Both are the signature of a `version` run that wrote and staged its changes but never committed -- the second covers a changeset that was only ever a working-tree file (added and consumed by `version` without ever being committed), which the first check cannot see. A repository with no commits yet, a manifest/changesets directory that didn't exist at `HEAD`, or an active pre-release cycle (which legitimately reruns `version` without a commit in between) is never refused this way.

By default, applying a plan refreshes each active ecosystem's lockfile that exists on disk: `cargo update --workspace` for Cargo; for Pypi, `uv lock` if `uv.lock` exists, else `poetry lock --no-update` if `poetry.lock` exists, else `pdm lock --update-reuse` if `pdm.lock` exists; for Npm, `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` for `package-lock.json`, `pnpm install --lockfile-only` for `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn install --mode update-lockfile` for `yarn.lock`, and `bun install --lockfile-only` for `bun.lock` or `bun.lockb`, each independently when its lockfile is present. `--no-refresh-lockfiles` skips this; `--refresh-lockfiles` is accepted but has no effect.
A lockfile refresh command that exits non-zero aborts `version` with E208 naming the lockfile and the exact command that failed, instead of recording the failure and continuing.
